question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gate is missing, but the permanent behavior defines a new authorization boundary and config contract across agent execution, tools, approvals, channels, Gateway scope, denial, timeout, and transcript handling.

options.title: Design core confirmation gate
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default core gate with deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and tests proving composition with existing plugin and exec approvals.

options.title: Keep policy plugin-only
options.body: Leave core behavior unchanged and require operators to implement contextual confirmation through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies, accepting that no built-in same-response gate exists.

options.title: Defer into broader policy model
options.body: Wait for the related action-level deny, response-gate, and HITL interrupt designs to settle before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design core confirmation gate
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default core gate with deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and tests proving composition with existing plugin and exec approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and the core agent execution loop, and prior live review already routed it to core product/security design.
